question: Will Darline Graham Nordone be the new republican nominee for Senate in South Carolina?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the special Republican Primary for United States Senator from South Carolina, including any potential runoff.

If no 2026 special South Carolina Republican Senate Primary takes place by November 2, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve according to the candidate who is the official Republican nominee to contest the November 3, 2026 South Carolina U.S. Senate election.

If the results of the special primary are not definitively known, or if there is no Republican nominee to contest the November 3, 2026 South Carolina U.S. Senate election, by November 2, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the South Carolina Republican party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.
research:
I could only use material dated on or before 2026-08-12. Most of my searches returned later articles, which I left out. Most page fetches failed because the proxy refused the connection, so many facts below come from search-result summaries and not from the full articles.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the South Carolina Republican Party's first announcement of the special primary winner, including any runoff. I could not find or fetch an official SCGOP results page.
- 2026-08-11: In the special Republican primary, Darline Graham (Nordone) finished first with 32.7%, Rep. Ralph Norman second with 24.6%, and Rep. Russell Fry third with about 20%. No one passed 50%, so South Carolina law requires a runoff between the top two. [Roll Call](https://rollcall.com/2026/08/11/darline-graham-will-face-ralph-norman-in-south-carolina-senate-runoff/); [NBC results](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-primary-special-elections/south-carolina-senate-results)
- The runoff between Graham Nordone and Norman is set for Tuesday, 2026-08-25. [Axios, 2026-08-12](https://axios.com/2026/08/12/south-carolina-gop-senate-graham-primary-runoff)

## 2. Current status
- The question is not settled yet. Graham Nordone is in a two-person runoff and finished about 8 points ahead of Norman in round one. Neither of them won a majority, and about 43% of first-round votes went to other candidates, mainly Fry. Where Fry's voters go is the key unknown.
- She is the sitting senator: Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her after her brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham, died on 2026-07-11. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darline_Graham)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-12: Axios reports the primary is going to a runoff. FITSNews ran a "winners and losers" piece and said Fry's endorsement decision is the next big test. [Axios](https://axios.com/2026/08/12/south-carolina-gop-senate-graham-primary-runoff); [FITSNews](https://www.fitsnews.com/2026/08/12/s-c-succession-winners-and-losers-from-the-u-s-senate-primary-election/)
- 2026-08-11: Primary night. Graham Nordone led with about 33% and Norman had about 24-25%. [Roll Call](https://rollcall.com/2026/08/11/darline-graham-will-face-ralph-norman-in-south-carolina-senate-runoff/)
- 2026-07-24: Graham Nordone formally filed to run. [FITSNews](https://www.fitsnews.com/2026/07/24/s-c-succession-darline-graham-nordone-files-to-run-for-u-s-senate/)
- 2026-07-20/21: She announced she would run for the full term. [Time](https://time.com/article/2026/07/20/darline-graham-nordone-lindsey-graham-senate-south-carolina-republican-primary/); [Deseret](https://www.deseret.com/politics/2026/07/21/darline-graham-nordone-announces-she-will-run-for-senate/)
- 2026-07-17: President Trump endorsed her. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/17/trump-darline-graham-nordone-senate-endorsement); [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/trump-backs-darline-graham-nordone-primary-replace-lindsey-graham-rcna588075)
- Opponents attacked her over her work at the state Commission for the Blind, including claims that she supported DEI policies. She disputed those claims. The general-election opponent is Democrat Annie Andrews.

## 4. Base rates
- I could not find a systematic study of South Carolina runoffs in the material I reviewed. Two general patterns that may be relevant, but which I did not verify here:
  - First-place finishers in Southern primary runoffs usually win, though not always.
  - Trump-endorsed candidates have a strong record in recent GOP primaries.
- In this race, the leader had only about 33% in round one, which leaves a lot of room for consolidation behind either candidate.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Early July 2026: Polymarket had Fry as the frontrunner at about 60% and Norman at about 18%. [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/lindsey-grahams-senate-replacement-what-the-odds-show-prediction-markets-12189879); [Lower Bucks Times](https://lowerbuckstimes.com/2026/07/14/south-carolina-senate-prediction-markets/)
- Mid/late July 2026: She took the prediction-market lead after Trump endorsed her. [DeFi Rate](https://defirate.com/?p=16519); [Federal News Network](https://federalnewsnetwork.com/prediction-markets/2026/07/odds-south-carolina-republican-senate-special-primary-who-will-replace-lindsay-graham/)
- About 2026-08-07/08, before the primary: Polymarket had Graham Nordone at about 46% and Fry at about 26%. [Newsweek](https://newsweek.com/grahams-chances-of-replacing-brother-on-south-carolina-ballot-after-debate-12280225)
- I could not find a Polymarket or Kalshi price for the runoff dated on or before 2026-08-12. Kalshi has a market on this race. [Kalshi News](https://news.kalshi.com/p/graham-norman-odds-south-carolina-senate-special-primary)
- I found no Manifold market or expert forecast for the runoff dated by the cutoff.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Endorsements from eliminated candidates, especially Fry, the third-place finisher with about 20%, and from other state Republicans.
- Any runoff debates, new polls and ad spending between 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-25.
- Further campaigning by Trump for Graham Nordone.
- 2026-08-25: Runoff election. After that come the AP call, the SCGOP announcement and certification.
- 2026-11-03: General election against Democrat Annie Andrews. This doesn't matter for resolution unless the nomination is still undecided by then.

**(d) Strongest evidence.**
- **For Yes:**
  - Trump endorsed her on 2026-07-17.
  - She led by 8 points on 2026-08-11.
  - She is the sitting senator, appointed by McMaster.
  - She led prediction markets before the primary (about 46% vs Fry 26%, around 2026-08-07).
  - Norman backed Haley over Trump in 2024. That probably limits his appeal to Fry's Trump-aligned voters.
- **For No:**
  - She won only about 33% in round one, so roughly 67% of voters chose someone else.
  - Opponents attacked her over DEI at the Commission for the Blind.
  - Runoff turnout drops and favors motivated activist voters, which can help a Freedom Caucus candidate like Norman.
  - Fry's endorsement was still pending as of 2026-08-12.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- **No:** Fry endorses Norman and frames the race as experience against a relatively unknown appointee. The "anyone but the appointed sister" vote consolidates, and low turnout favors Norman's activist base. Norman wins 52-48.
- **Yes:** Trump rallies or does tele-town-halls for her, Fry stays neutral or backs the Trump pick, and she wins comfortably, around 58-42.

**(f) Adjustment.** I start at about 70%. I move up about 7 points for the Trump endorsement combined with Norman's anti-Trump history in 2024, since that combination should pull Fry voters toward her. I don't move higher because her first-round share was low and the Fry endorsement is still unknown. There is no runoff market price to anchor on.

Probability: 77%

  - Trump endorsed her on 2026-07-17, which moved prediction markets sharply toward her.

(f) **Final probability.** I start at about 68%. I move up modestly, to about 72%, for the Trump endorsement and for Norman's Haley baggage with Fry-type voters. I hold back from going higher because her weak first-round share leaves room for a consolidated opposition.
